name: Vanquish Request a Quote for WooCommerce
author: Vanquish

sections.description:
Vanquish Request a Quote for WooCommerce lets your customers ask for a price instead of buying straight away. They add products to a quote list, send it with a short form, and you answer with your prices. Once you accept the quote, the customer pays it online like any other order.

A quote is a WooCommerce order with its own statuses, so everything you already know keeps working: you edit prices, quantities, shipping and discounts on the order screen, the customer pays with the payment methods of your store, and the paid quote carries on as a normal order.

How it goes:

  1. The customer clicks Add to quote on the products they are interested in, in the shop or on the product page.
  2. On the quote page they review the list, fill in the form and send the request. They do not need an account.
  3. You get an email and find the request under Quotes in your admin. You set your prices and accept it, or reject it.
  4. The customer gets your quote by email, with a button to pay it. Customers with an account also find it under My account → Quotes.

It works with simple and variable products, with any payment method, and with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage).

Free features

  • An Add to quote button in the shop and on the product page, with your own text, and a shortcode to place it anywhere: [vanqt_add_to_quote id="123"].
  • A quote list with thumbnails, SKUs and quantities, and a quote page with the request form, created for you when you activate the plugin. Show the form below the list or beside it.
  • A link to the quote list with a counter in the menu you choose, and as a shortcode: [vanqt_quote_link].
  • Choose what can be quoted: every product, or only the products you tick on the product screen. Products without a price can be quoted too.
  • Show or hide prices on the products that can be quoted, and keep or remove “Add to cart” on them: sell and quote side by side, or work on price on request only.
  • A request form with name, email, phone and message, and an optional privacy checkbox linked to your privacy policy.
  • Guests can ask for a quote, and pay it from the link in the email, without creating an account.
  • Quote statuses of their own: New quote request, Quote accepted, Quote rejected, and more, in a Quotes screen with Accept / Reject buttons, a counter of the new requests, and an Add quote button to write a quote from scratch.
  • Payment of the accepted quote through the checkout of your store. Once it is paid, the quote becomes a normal order and the usual WooCommerce emails go out.
  • My account → Quotes for the customer: the list of their quotes and each quote in detail, with a Pay button when there is something to pay.
  • Four emails, managed in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails like any other: New quote request to you, and Quote request received, Quote accepted (with the Pay button) and Quote rejected to the customer.
  • Spam protection that needs no account anywhere: a hidden trap field and a limit on how often a visitor can send. Google reCAPTCHA v2 is there too if you want it.
  • The quote list survives page caching: nothing personal is written in the page itself.
  • Every text translatable; template overrides from your theme.
  • Migrates automatically from the CodeCanyon plugin “WooCommerce Quote”: your settings are imported and your quotes keep working, with nothing to convert.

Premium features

  • Rules for what can be quoted — by category (with or without its subcategories), by tag, by single variation, every product except the ones you list, and automatically for products that are out of stock or have no price.
  • Rules for who can ask — by user role, guests included.
  • Turn the cart into a quote — a button in the cart sends its whole content as a quote request, options added by other plugins included.
  • Your own request form — add, remove and reorder fields: text, email, phone, text area, drop-down, multiple choice, checkbox, date, time and country. Half or full width, required or not, and copied to the order field you choose (company, billing or shipping address, customer note).
  • Expiry and automation — accepted quotes expire after the time you set and can no longer be paid; a reminder email goes out before they do; requests you have not answered in time can be accepted automatically. Set a different expiry date, and write a message, on each single quote.
  • The customer can reject the quote, giving a reason, and you are told by email.
  • A thank-you page of your choice after the request is sent.
  • Webhook — the quote is sent as JSON to an address you choose when it is created, when its status changes and when it is paid, signed so that the receiver can check where it comes from. Use it with Zapier, Make, n8n or your CRM.
  • Your own sender — a “From” name and address for the quote emails only.
  • Your own wording, in every language — rewrite the buttons, the headings, the notices and each email’s subject, heading and message, with placeholders such as the quote number, the total, the expiry date and the payment link, in each language of a WPML, Polylang or Falang site.

External services

This plugin can use Google reCAPTCHA v2 to protect the request form from spam. It is off by default: nothing is loaded from Google and nothing is sent to it unless you turn it on under Quotes → Settings and enter your keys. When it is on, the quote page loads Google’s reCAPTCHA script, which runs in the visitor’s browser and talks to Google from there, and when a request is sent your site sends Google the response token produced by that script, together with your secret key, to verify it. The service is provided by Google: terms of service, privacy policy.

This plugin uses Freemius to manage licensing and updates for the premium version, and to offer an optional opt-in when you first activate it. Nothing is sent unless you opt in or activate a licence; if you do, Freemius receives your site URL, WordPress and PHP versions and your administrator email address, in order to deliver updates and support. See freemius.com, its terms and its privacy policy.

The premium version can send each quote to a webhook address that you enter yourself (your CRM, Zapier, Make and so on). It is empty by default and nothing is sent until you fill it in. When you do, the quote’s number, status, total and products, the customer’s name, company, email and phone, their note and the answers given in the request form are sent to that address when a quote is created, changes status or is paid. That address is your own choice, so its terms and privacy policy are those of the service you point it at.

More WooCommerce plugins by Vanquish

  • Vanquish Order Approval for WooCommerce – review every order before it goes ahead, and let the customer pay before or after you approve it. Where this plugin is about agreeing on a price, Order Approval is about deciding whether an order can go ahead.
  • Vanquish Upload Files for WooCommerce – let customers upload files (even large ones) on the product, cart, checkout and order pages, for custom, personalized and print-on-demand products.
  • Vanquish Shipping Tracking for WooCommerce – tracking numbers on orders and emails, with 1,600+ carriers and their logos, a direct tracking link and a Track button. No account needed.
  • Vanquish Multiple Addresses for WooCommerce – give customers an address book: save multiple billing and shipping addresses and pick one at checkout.
  • Vanquish Attach Me for WooCommerce – attach any file to any order or product, show it to the customer and send it with the order emails.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/vanquish-request-a-quote-for-woocommerce directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Make sure WooCommerce is installed and active.
  4. That is all it takes to start: every product gets an Add to quote button, and a “Request a quote” page is created for you. Go to Quotes → Settings to choose which products can be quoted, whether their prices are shown, and which menu gets the link to the quote list.
sections.faq:
How does the customer get the price and pay?

The request arrives with the prices of your shop, or with no price for the products that have none. You open it under Quotes, set the price of each line as you would on any order, add shipping or a discount if you need to, and click Accept. The customer receives the “Quote accepted” email with your prices and a Pay button, which leads to the payment page of your store. Customers with an account can also pay from My account → Quotes.

Do customers need an account to ask for a quote?

No. A guest fills in the form and receives the emails like anyone else, and the link in the email opens their quote and lets them pay it.

Can I sell some products normally and quote others?

Yes. Under Quotes → Settings choose “Only for the products I select” and tick Can be quoted on the product screen of the ones you want. The other products are not touched. On the products that can be quoted you decide whether the price is shown and whether “Add to cart” stays next to “Add to quote”.

Can I hide prices and work on price on request only?

Yes. Under Quotes → Settings, switch off “Show the price of products that can be quoted” and “Products that can be quoted can also be bought the normal way”: the products that can be quoted show no price and can only be added to the quote list.

The “Add to quote” button does not appear in my shop or on a page built with a page builder.

The button is added through the standard WooCommerce hooks, which most themes run. Product grids made of blocks, and pages laid out with a page builder, often do not run them. In those places use the shortcode: [vanqt_add_to_quote] inside a product page, or [vanqt_add_to_quote id="123"] anywhere, with the ID of the product.

Where is the quote list, and can I link to it?

It is on the “Request a quote” page the plugin created when you activated it, which you can rename or replace with any page containing the [vanqt_request_quote] shortcode. Under Quotes → Settings you choose a menu to add a link with a counter to, and [vanqt_quote_link] prints the same link wherever you put it.

Can I create a quote myself, for a customer who called or wrote to me?

Yes. The Add quote button on the Quotes screen opens a new order in the “New quote request” status: add the customer and the products, set your prices and accept it. The customer gets the same email with the Pay button.

Does it work with page caching?

Yes. The pages are the same for every visitor: the counter and the state of the buttons are filled in by a small request after the page has loaded, and only for visitors who have something in their list.

Does it work with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage)?

Yes, with HPOS and with the classic order storage.

I am migrating from the CodeCanyon “WooCommerce Quote” plugin. Do I lose anything?

No. The quote statuses have the same names, so every quote — new, accepted, rejected, expired or long paid — keeps its status and history with nothing to convert. Your settings are imported automatically the first time the new plugin runs, and Quotes → Settings → Import from the old plugin shows what was imported, which of the functions you were using are now part of Premium, and the two that are no longer there. The old plugin’s data is never changed or deleted, so you can always go back.

The two plugins drive the same statuses, so they cannot run together: while the old one is active the new one waits and says so. Deactivate the old one and everything carries on.

Can I change the wording the customer sees?

The text of the “Add to quote” button is a setting. The other texts are translatable like any other plugin’s, and each email’s subject, heading and additional content are edited in WooCommerce → Settings → Emails. Premium adds a Texts screen to rewrite the buttons, the notices and the email messages, per language.

Do the premium features change how the free ones behave?

No. The premium package is the same plugin with more in it. Everything described above under “free features” works the same either way, and the settings you have already made are untouched by activating a licence.

How much does Premium cost, and how do I get it?

There are monthly, yearly and lifetime plans, for one site up to ten.

To see the current prices and to order, install and activate the free version, then go to Quotes → Upgrade in your WordPress admin. The plans and a secure checkout, handled by Freemius, are right there, and the same screen walks you through activating Premium on your site.

Can I try the plugin before buying Premium?

Yes, and it is the best way to start. The free version on WordPress.org is the same plugin with fewer features: install it on your own site, with your own theme and payment methods, and check that the Add to quote button, the quote page and the quote emails fit your shop before upgrading. Premium adds features on top of it, on the same foundations.

What happens if I uninstall the plugin?

Nothing of yours is removed: your settings and your quotes, with their statuses, stay as they are, so reinstalling puts you back exactly where you were. Only the plugin’s scheduled events and caches go.
sections.changelog:
1.0.3

  • New: hooks for other plugins: a line added to or removed from the quote list, the list emptied, a check before a request becomes a quote, the form of a product that can only be quoted, and a JavaScript event after a product is added. They are what Upload Files for WooCommerce uses to bring its files to quotes.
  • Tweak: the status names and the Add quote button are called in this readme as they are in the plugin.

1.0.2

  • Tweak: the plugin icon has a new colour, matching the new look of the plugin page.

1.0.1

  • Fixed (Premium): on a store migrated from the CodeCanyon plugin, quotes accepted with the old plugin were marked as expired as soon as Premium was activated, when the date the old plugin had stored for them was in the past. Only an expiry date set by this plugin counts now; those quotes stay as they are, and get a deadline when you accept them again or set one yourself.

1.0.0

  • First release, replacing the CodeCanyon plugin “WooCommerce Quote”.
